description: All three openCARP calibration-gate attempts, preserved. Each run of scripts/opencarp_calibrate.py overwrote results/opencarp_calibration.json, so the two rejected configurations survived only in the commit log and lab notebook. The manuscript cites the rejected rates as evidence the gate could fail, so they need a stored source.

gate_criteria.note: Band and sign are the section 7.4 calibration gate, defined on the Roney cohort before openCARP was available.

discipline: Every change between attempts was anchored to an INDEPENDENT physiological target (APD90, then conduction velocity), never to the gate itself. No endpoint parameter (reentry_min_ms, max_depol_fraction, min_reactivating_nodes) was altered at any stage, which is why the gate remained able to fail.

attempts.configuration: openCARP defaults: tau_close 150, tau_out 5; g_il 0.174, g_it 0.019; fibrosis reduces CONDUCTIVITY only
attempts.diagnosis: A negative fibrosis-verdict correlation is the signature of rate-dependent block rather than reentry. Fibrosis was reducing conductivity but not shortening the action potential, so added fibrosis could only add block.

attempts.configuration: fibrosis-dependent ERP added: tau_close = 115 x (1 - 0.5 f), tau_out 6, tau_in 0.3, tau_open 120, V_gate 0.13; conductivity still at openCARP defaults
attempts.diagnosis: Improved but still failing, so the ERP omission was only part of the cause. Conduction velocity had never been calibrated: the shipped conductivity gives CV 0.344 m/s against the frozen 0.4-1.2 m/s band, a ~75 mm wavelength in an atrium of ~110 mm characteristic length, which makes reentry trivially easy.

attempts.configuration: conduction velocity also calibrated: g_il 1.05, g_it 0.315, g_el 3.78, g_et 1.134 -> CV ~0.87 m/s; transverse at 0.3x longitudinal to match the in-house along/cross weighting

uw.note: correlation undefined with no variance in the verdict

attempts.diagnosis: ACCEPTED for Roney. Rate mid-band and the fibrosis-verdict correlation strongly positive, against the frozen solver's 0.75. openCARP calls inducible where monodomain does not in zero cases, so it is the more conservative solver.

measured_calibration_curves.note: CV first appeared to saturate because the monodomain conductivity is the harmonic mean of intra- and extracellular values; raising g_il alone asymptotes at g_el. The curve above is with both scaled together.
